results.text:
Talk about making love before you do it

Most couples don’t talk honestly about sex until they’re already having it. Bad timing. Once you’re naked, saying what you actually want can interrupt the whole thing or disappoint the person right in front of you. Talk before you’re naked. That conversation is already part of making love.

I want to know what actually makes her body relax and open, and she should know the same about me. Is there anything kinky that one of us needs to be able to say out loud? Has the past made us want certain things or avoid them? What just doesn't work?

Maybe we don't know all of that yet. “I don’t know, but I’m willing to find out honestly with you” is a perfectly good answer.

We may not even mean the same thing by sex. I may mostly think bonding and she may mostly think play. Sometimes it may feel sacred; another time it may just be how we come down from a bad day. It doesn't have to mean the same thing every time.

Sex drive doesn't stay put, either. For some stretch one of us is going to want more, less, or something different. That's one of the saddest places for quiet resentment to grow. I'd rather talk about what we'll do when that happens before either person is already hurt. We can't solve a future mismatch in advance, but at least we'll have somewhere to begin.

And then can we still say all this once we're naked? If I think she'll be disappointed, can I tell her anyway? If not, we're just hoping sex will sort out what we didn't want to say.

Bodies fitting isn't enough. I want to know whether we can stay honest while we're completely exposed. Talking before our clothes come off is already practicing that.

From here on, when I say making love, I'm talking about two people who care about each other deeply and feel super connected, using their bodies as part of that connection. If you’ve never experienced this, it may be like trying to explain the taste of an orange. If you don’t know what love is, you don’t know. That’s another conversation, and I'd suggest reading my inner child reparenting guide.
